title: My first Experience with Ai game development
author: Finn_Karak
selftext:
Hello AI game devs,

This is my first post on this platform, and after seeing the progress so many of you have made, I decided to share some of my own progress as well.

I personally had absolutely no idea how to write code myself when I started. But after working on this project for around three months, I have slowly learned enough to at least understand code on a basic level.

So, here is my story.

I am a huge fan of board games, especially Karak. It is a game that, on the surface, has some similarities to DnD. You play with 2–5 people and explore a dungeon step by step, fight enemies, collect loot and search for treasure.

Every game feels a little different, and because you randomly choose different heroes with different abilities at the beginning of each game, it often feels like you are experiencing your own little adventure and story.

But after playing it many, many times, that feeling slowly disappeared. At some point, you have simply seen and experienced almost everything the game has to offer.

That is when I got the idea to try developing my own game, which would still be inspired by the basic concept of Karak, but could grow far beyond it.

And that is where my journey started.

At first, I sat down with Claude and built a basic framework for the game. I was honestly fascinated by how quickly we were able to create something and how well it worked.

Then the user limits arrived...

And my project basically froze.

About a week later, I decided to try again. This time I started working with ChatGPT and OpenCode. By combining both AIs, I managed to recreate the basic game.

But once that worked, I started getting more and more ideas for things I could add beyond the original board game.

Here is a small overview of some of the things I have already added:

* A custom XP and leveling system with increasing requirements and character progression
* A talent tree with different progression paths
* A much more advanced combat system instead of simply copying the original Karak combat system, which I am currently still working on
* Different weapon classes with their own abilities, such as staffs, greatswords and more
* A loot system with weapon quality, rarities and affixes
* A larger inventory and equipment system with different equipment slots
* More enemy types with their own HP values and characteristics
* Spells and active abilities that can be used tactically during combat
* Healing fountains, traps, portals, chests and other special tiles/events
* A death and respawn system instead of relying purely on the original board game mechanics
* A compendium where enemies, items and other discovered content can be collected
* A complete overworld in addition to the classic dungeon system
* And even my own world editor engine

And I still have a lot more ideas.

There are so many things I would still love to add.

At the moment, the main things slowing me down are usage limits and some of the more capable models being locked behind paywalls.

I mainly wanted to share this little adventure because I do not really have anyone in my personal circle who is even remotely interested in game development or this project.

Maybe someone here finds the project interesting or has more experience with AI-assisted game development and could share some advice with me.

Especially because I know that the way I am currently working is probably not the most optimal or efficient workflow yet.

Feel free to ask me anything if something is unclear or if you want to know more about the project.

I would love to hear your thoughts and comments :)

Anyway you did most important thing. Started and got results and got ideas! Thats great goid luck!

replies.author: Finn_Karak
replies.body:
Tysm.   
At the moment, my workflow is basically that I use ChatGPT to design the prompts for OpenCode. This way, OpenCode does not waste its usage limits by constantly rereading all the project files and already knows exactly where something needs to be changed, added or checked.
